title: Replication Codebase: Customs aggregation and scarcity pricing drive a trillion-dollar global threatened seafood trade
description:
Clean, reproducible Python analytical and econometric codebase for the research article: "Customs aggregation and scarcity pricing drive a trillion-dollar global threatened seafood trade" (submitted to Nature Sustainability).

Important Note on Data Distribution: In strict adherence to repository scope, institutional terms of use, and open-science best practices, no raw microdata or processed empirical datasets are distributed in this archive. All primary datasets are publicly accessible from their respective international institutional repositories (UN Comtrade, CEPII BACI, IUCN Red List API v4, CITES Secretariat, World Customs Organization, FishBase, SeaLifeBase, FAO FishStatJ, World Bank WDI/WGI/CWON, Quality of Government Institute, WTO Tariff Download Facility, OECD Fisheries Support Estimates, Global Fishing Watch, and RAM Legacy Stock Assessment Database v4.44). All aggregated empirical summaries, statistical tables, and model outputs supporting the study are published directly in the article and Supplementary Information (Supplementary Tables S1–S20).

This archive contains exclusively the 13 core analytical Python modules (01–13) used to generate the empirical estimates, bioeconomic models, and optimization solutions reported in the manuscript: species-to-HS6 conservation concordances, Taxonomic Aggregation Ratio (TAR) and Species Customs Resolution Index (SCRI) audits, WCO HS 2028 legal amendment verification, Dual-IV scarcity pricing and wild-versus-farmed price tests, coupled wild-aquaculture differential-equation bifurcations and Pontryagin stochastic optimal control, Comparative Interrupted Time Series and zero-retaining Structural Gravity PPML estimations, bilateral mirror evasion and Stackelberg border inspection models, live-weight-equivalent marine trophic accounting, sovereign governance partial-derivative suites, non-circular 0–1 binary mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) tariff disaggregation optimization, and bilevel port network interdiction with Monte Carlo Shapley allocation.

Author: Sezgin Tunca (Department of Business and Sustainability, University of Southern Denmark, Odense, Denmark; ORCID: 0000-0001-6840-1466).
